title: Synchronous and Asynchronous Endpoints
subtopics: Avoiding blocking work in asynchronous endpoints
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of synchronous and asynchronous endpoints in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to normal def path operations.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers synchronous and asynchronous endpoints within asynchronous programming and concurrency. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use synchronous and asynchronous endpoints to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is resource lifecycle, cancellation, concurrency limits and observable I/O behavior.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Synchronous and Asynchronous Endpoints matters because it is part of asynchronous programming and concurrency. In practice, focus on resource lifecycle, cancellation, concurrency limits and observable I/O behavior. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Normal def path operations
items.text: Use normal def path operations as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: async def path operations
items.text: For async def path operations, identify which operation waits on I/O, which resources remain open, and what happens on timeout or disconnect. Async syntax does not make CPU-bound work faster or durable background jobs reliable by itself.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
